## Keywords

{{< glossary slide-layout placeholder theme designer colour-contrast speaker-notes slide-transition slide-animation >}}

## 8.1 Slides and layouts

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A layout is the plan of a slide.
- Its placeholders are dashed boxes where we click and type.
- The first slide uses Title Slide, and most slides use Title and Content.
- **Lab task:** Make a title slide and a content slide. Which key starts the show?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/layouts.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Layouts

a) What is the dashed box "Click to add title" called?
b) Which layout fits the first slide of a talk?
c) Which layout puts a list next to a picture?

::: {.answer}
a) a placeholder
b) Title Slide
c) Two Content
:::

## 8.2 Themes and Designer

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A theme gives all slides the same colours and fonts.
- Designer suggests designs for the slide we are on.
- Dark text on light, or light text on dark, gives strong contrast.
- **Lab task:** Choose a theme and two Variants. Can you read it from two metres?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/themes.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · Themes

a) On which tab do we choose a theme?
b) What changes when we click a theme?
c) Why is light grey text on light blue a problem?

::: {.answer}
a) Design
b) the colours and fonts of all slides
c) Nobody at the back can read it.
:::

## 8.3 Few words and speaker notes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Each slide has one idea and 3 to 5 short points.
- Each point has about eight words or fewer.
- What we say goes into the speaker notes under the slide.
- **Lab task:** Shorten your points. Which details did you move into the notes?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/text-amount.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · Few words and notes

a) How many points should a slide have?
b) Where do you write what you will say?
c) Who sees the speaker notes in the slide show?

::: {.answer}
a) 3 to 5 short points
b) in the speaker notes, under the slide
c) only the speaker, in Presenter View
:::

## 8.4 Transitions and animations

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A transition is the way one slide changes to the next.
- An animation makes one thing on a slide appear or move.
- One quiet transition for all slides is enough.
- **Lab task:** Add Fade to all slides and Appear to one list. What happens on each click?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/animation-steps.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 4 · Transitions and animations

a) Which button gives every slide the same transition?
b) How long should a transition be?
c) What do you add when the points of a list must come one by one?

::: {.answer}
a) Apply To All
b) 0.5 to 1 second
c) an animation, By Paragraph
:::

## Game challenge · Slide Doctor

{{< sim file="sims/slide-doctor.html" poster="sims/slide-doctor.png" title="Slide Doctor: fix the slide" kind="game" task="**The story:** Huda's colleagues send slides for the Monday meeting, and each one has a problem. **Play:** choose the best fix for each slide." >}}

## Try it 5 · Fix the slide (harder)

The facts: one slide has seven long sentences, and the shop photo looks tall and thin. The detail "Rana puts a notice on the door" is on a slide.

a) What is the best fix for a slide with seven long sentences?
b) What went wrong with the shop photo that looks tall and thin?
c) Where does "Rana puts a notice on the door" go?

::: {.answer}
a) Keep a few short points and say the rest.
b) It was stretched with a side handle.
c) in the speaker notes
:::

## Summary

- We choose a layout and type in its placeholders.
- One theme gives the whole talk one look with strong contrast.
- Each slide has one idea and a few short points, and the notes keep the rest.
- One quiet transition and a simple animation help the audience follow.
- We resize pictures from a corner and give them alt text.
